judgment.rationale: Both Content SFIs sit under Competency C-3.2 ("Describes location and movement using common and mathematical language; understands the concept of a map") within CG-3, and both address route maps (shared LC tags location/map/route). The Class-3 item (rank 2) has learners describe position and location within one simple, familiar route map (home to school); the Class-4 item (rank 3) requires actively tracing routes for arbitrary given locations. This is a substantive extension from reading/describing positions on a single given map to generating and tracing routes between varied specified locations, so facility with describing position and location on a simple route map supports success at tracing routes, in the lower-to-higher Class-3 to Class-4 direction. Shared parentage and page proximity alone were not treated as sufficient; the decision rests on the pair-specific content progression. judgment.rationale: Both are Class-4 Content statements (rank 3, same coordinate) under the shared Curricular Goal CG-4 on measuring attributes and relating measure to number, but they sit under different competencies: the first ('Measurement-related application problems using addition and subtraction', LCs on solving measurement word problems with addition/subtraction, under C-4.3 unit conversion and everyday problem solving) and the second ('Measuring length of the objects (centimetre) using a scale', LC on measuring length in centimetres with a scale, under C-4.2 selecting suitable units and tools). They are substantively coherent — instrument-based length measurement produces the quantities that measurement application problems operate on, and both share the 'measurement' LC tag — but at the same class rank the evidence does not establish that proficiency in one substantively supports success in the other: the arithmetic application content spans measurement attributes generally and is not scoped to scale-based length measurement, and the shared tokens ('using', 'measurement') are generic. Conceptual/complementary coherence without justified developmental dependency supports a symmetric relatesTo. Evidence is bounded: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (33 and 24 omitted items) and ancestors carry merge/audit context, so a stronger developmental reading could not be confirmed.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same data-handling Competency C-5.1 ('Collects data ... represents it in tabular form ... and interprets it'). The Class-3 item (rank 2) has learners use tally marks to collect data, answer questions and classify by grouping; the Class-4 item (rank 3) moves to recording data more generally, i.e. systematic entry/organisation of collected data. Hands-on tallying, grouping and questioning of collected data is the concrete precursor skill that supports success in recording data at the next class level, so the direction is lower-to-higher rank (Class-3 -> Class-4). This is substantive extension of the same data-handling strand, not merely shared wording ('data') or shared page/parent. Note the Class-4 statement is terse and its source evidence is truncated, limiting detail about the recording formats intended.

The 'numbers up to 999' phrasing appears only in a shared table_row[4] context label that is reproduced verbatim in both endpoints' candidate_source_refs, so it cannot be attributed to the Class-3 endpoint alone; the upstream merge note about not merging Content across classes is an extraction-identity rule rather than pair-specific evidence of increased complexity. judgment.rationale: Both are Class-4 (rank 3) Content SFIs under Competency C-2.2 (representing and comparing common fractions as parts of a whole). The first, 'Dividing the given shape into equal parts' (LC: 'Divide a given shape into equal parts'), establishes equal partitioning of a shape; the second, 'Fractional parts by shading and colouring' (LC: 'Represent fractional parts of a whole by shading and colouring'), requires that partitioned whole in order to shade a specified number of the equal parts and thereby name a fractional quantity. This is a pair-specific extension from partitioning to representing/naming a fraction on the partitioned shape, so proficiency with equal partitioning supports success with shading fractional parts; the same-rank direction rests on this substantive content dependency rather than on shared parent, page 3 proximity, or the 'parts'/'fractions' token overlap alone. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (32 omitted source-evidence items each) and both, plus their ancestors, carry upstream merge context (duplicate extraction across overlapping windows), though the merged duplicates do not conflict in content; the coordinate-less ancestors are context only and contribute no rank.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same Competency C-2.3 (relationships among operations) and Curricular Goal CG-2. The Class-3 item covers constructing division facts through equal sharing/grouping and repeated subtraction (LCs: construct division facts by equal sharing/grouping; by repeated subtraction), while the Class-4 item covers skip counting and constructing multiplication tables of 6, 7, 8 and 9 (LCs: skip count by 6-9; construct those tables). These are substantively coherent as inverse equal-group reasoning — repeated subtraction/equal grouping mirrors skip counting/repeated addition — so they reinforce one another conceptually. However, the evidence does not support a developmental dependency in the only permitted direction: constructing division facts is not shown to be needed for, or to prepare, the construction of multiplication tables of 6-9 (if anything the table work would normally underpin division facts). Shared ancestry, adjacent class rank, page proximity, and generic token overlap ('and', 'construction') are not by themselves developmental evidence, so symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content SFIs under CG-2 (fluency with whole numbers). The first (Class-3, rank 2) is 'Plays with numbers and identifies patterns', with LCs 'Play with numbers' and 'Identify patterns in numbers'. The second (Class-5, rank 4) is 'Factors and common factors', sitting under competency C-2.5 ('Identifies, describes and extends simple number patterns...'), with LCs 'Identify factors of a given number' and 'Identify common factors of two numbers'. Direction is lower-to-higher rank and the change is substantive rather than mere repetition: informal number play and pattern recognition with whole numbers is extended into a specific multiplicative-structure topic (factors and shared factors of two numbers), so proficiency in exploring numbers and spotting numerical patterns plausibly supports success with factor work. judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under Competency C-4.2 (selecting units/tools for measuring attributes and evaluating conservation of length and volume). The first (Class-3, rank 2; LC 'Evaluate the conservation of length') establishes the conceptual understanding that an object's length is invariant under repositioning; the second (Class-4, rank 3; LC 'Measure the length of objects in centimetre using a scale') applies length measurement with a standard unit and instrument. Grasping conservation of length supports reliable, meaningful scale-based centimetre measurement, so the lower-to-higher direction is developmentally supported, not mere wording overlap ('length'). Note that supplied source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so this judgment rests on the bounded descriptions, LCs, and shared C-4.2/CG-4 measurement context.
